messages:
sophia: quick heads-up — i've put together a prototype for a 'contingency policy wizard' in the console. it bundles automatic fallback triggers, degrade modes, and audit controls into a single flow. would love quick feedback on the UX and any API limits we need to consider.

rajiv: skimmed — nice. question: do we let users compose multiple triggers (eg: 5xx rate OR p95 latency > 1.2s)? or only a single composite rule?

hannah: we should support AND/OR nesting. product teams will want complex guardrails. BUT the UI needs to stay simple — maybe an "advanced mode" for nested logic.

kevin: from infra POV nesting is fine as long as we translate to a flat matcher tree in the runtime. prefer keeping execution semantics deterministic. also need to cap rule evaluation cost for high QPS routes.

sophia: noted. proposal: allow a visual builder with default simple clauses (status, error-type, latency percentile, quota breach) and an "add condition" toggle. advanced mode exposes grouping + not operator.

design-bot: mock uploaded: https://redwood.internal/designs/contingency-wizard/v1 — it shows a policy preview + simulation pane (live traffic replay). thoughts? :eyes:

hannah: love the simulation pane. request: include a sample payload and a small distribution histogram so teams can eyeball what fraction of traffic would match before enabling.

rajiv: +1. also an API-first model: every policy created via console should map 1:1 to an internal policy object we can CRUD via admin API. we can't have console-only behaviors.

kevin: agreed. API shape suggestion (very rough):

```
{
  "policy_id": "guid",
  "matchers": [ { "type": "http_status", "op": "gte", "value": 500 }, { "type": "latency_p95", "op": ">", "value": 1200 } ],
  "combiner": "OR",
  "degrade_mode": "partial_cache|model_variant|reject",
  "rollout": { "percent": 10, "stages": ["canary", "global"] },
  "audit": { "retention_days": 90, "log_level": "trace" }
}
```

sophia: that's great. couple of UX questions: 1) do we show cost impact estimate for degrade_mode choices? 2) how granular is the rollout (per-route, per-model, per-customer)?

kevin: cost estimate is doable with heuristics (tokens saved via cache vs model_variant token delta). rollout granularity: allow per-route + per-model. customer-scoped policies should be gated behind entitlements.

hannah: for audit: default retention should be moderate (30d) but with an enterprise option 365d. UI should show storage and egress warnings if they choose long retention.

rajiv: on triggers — need to standardize signal names across runtime telemetry: use p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate_5m, http_5xx_rate, model_fail_rate, kv_cache_miss_rate. console should offer friendly labels but map to canonical signals.

sophia: good call. also we need an explicit "escape hatch" in the policy: immediate disable button and an automatic rollback to previous policy version on sustained errors. how should that appear?

design-bot: proposal: top-right small pill "escape hatch" enabled by default for auto policies. clicking opens a confirm modal with reason + optional slack/email notify toggles. we also added an auto-rollback checkbox with a threshold (minutes).

kevin: implementational note: auto-rollback needs to persist previous policy snapshot and a monotonic backoff for re-enables. also track why it rolled back for audit.

audit-bot: FYI — any policy that affects production routing must create an audit entry with: actor, diff, simulated_impact (if available), and a runbook link. retention applies per policy.

hannah: simulation -> can we support a "what-if" that shows token-level cost delta per day/week? even a ballpark number helps ops/product evaluate tradeoffs.

rajiv: that requires running sampled traffic through the candidate policy against a lightweight model-cost estimator. not cheap, but we can do async jobs and cache results for 24h. surface status in the UI.

sophia: ok plan of record:
- console: visual builder (simple + advanced) with matchers mapped to canonical telemetry signals
- simulation pane: sample distribution, match rate, and estimated cost delta (async job)
- API parity: every console action writes a policy object to admin API, versioned
- audit: mandatory audit entry with diff + actor + simulated_impact (when available)
- escape hatch + auto-rollback with snapshotting

kevin: agree, also add quota guardrail: if a policy would increase downstream cost beyond X% in 24h, warn and require a secondary approval.

hannah: UX nit: when users create a policy we should show a "preview traffic fraction" slider to set rollout percent and a baked-in recommendation (e.g., start at 1% for risky changes).

rajiv: access control: policies should accept a metadata "scope" field and respect RBAC — only routes owners can edit per-route policies. enterprise admins can bump global fallbacks.

sophia: can someone volunteer to wire the admin API contract + simulation job ticket? i'm happy to take the console bits with hannah/design.

rajiv: i'll take the admin API contract and write spec. i'll include sample JSON, error responses, and pagination for listing policies.

kevin: i'll spike the simulation job infra and a cost estimator stub. give me one sprint.

hannah: i'll iterate the mocks and add the histogram + preview slider.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment created for feature/contingency-wizard-api (id: canary-4782). automatic tests queued.

sophia: perfect. follow-ups: add runbook templates for common degrade modes, and a short doc for SRE on interpreting simulation output. i'll create a GH issue and link design + rfc.

kevin: one last thought — telemetry cardinality. if users build many complex policies we should limit number of unique matchers per org to avoid explosion in metric tags. propose default 100 unique matcher variants/org and warn after 75.

hannah: noted, will add UI warning.

sophia: thanks all. we'll sync Friday 10am to review API spec + mocks. cc @rajiv @kevin @hannah

kevin: :thumbsup:

rajiv: :+1:

audit-bot: policy creation audit queued (policy_id placeholder) — retention defaults to 30d.
